name: Cairo & Giza
tagline: The pyramids, the treasures of the pharaohs and the Nile at night.
summary: Egypt's capital is where most trips begin. The Giza plateau sits on the edge of the city, the great museums hold the finds from every period of ancient Egypt, and old Cairo's bazaars and mosques are a world of their own.
bestTime: October to April — warm days, cool evenings.

highlights.title: Pyramids of Giza & the Sphinx
highlights.text: The Great Pyramid of Khufu (about 2560 BC) is the last standing wonder of the ancient world. Go early to beat the heat and the crowds.

highlights.title: Egyptian Museum & Grand Egyptian Museum
highlights.text: The historic Tahrir museum is packed with statues and coffins; the Grand Egyptian Museum beside the pyramids displays Tutankhamun's treasures together.

highlights.title: Saqqara & Memphis
highlights.text: Djoser's Step Pyramid — the oldest of Egypt's pyramids — and the ruins of the first capital, an easy half-day from Giza.

highlights.title: Islamic Cairo & Khan el-Khalili
highlights.text: Medieval mosques, the Citadel of Saladin and a bazaar that has traded since the 14th century.

highlights.title: The Nile by night
highlights.text: A felucca sail at sunset or a dinner cruise along the lit-up riverbanks.

gallery.caption: The Sphinx and the pyramid of Khafre

name: Luxor & Aswan
tagline: Temples, royal tombs and the slow, beautiful Nile.
summary: Ancient Thebes was the religious heart of the New Kingdom, and Luxor still holds more monuments than anywhere else in Egypt. Upriver, Aswan is calmer — granite islands, Nubian villages and the gateway to Abu Simbel. A Nile cruise links the two.
bestTime: October to April. Summer afternoons regularly pass 40 °C.

highlights.title: Karnak & Luxor Temple
highlights.text: Karnak's hall of 134 giant columns, and Luxor Temple lit up after dark — joined by the restored Avenue of Sphinxes.

highlights.title: Valley of the Kings
highlights.text: Painted royal tombs cut into the West Bank hills, including Tutankhamun's.

highlights.title: Temple of Hatshepsut
highlights.text: The terraced temple of Egypt's most powerful female pharaoh, set against the cliffs of Deir el-Bahari.

highlights.title: Abu Simbel & Philae
highlights.text: Ramses II's colossal temples, moved block by block in the 1960s to escape Lake Nasser, and the island temple of Isis at Aswan.

highlights.title: Nile cruise
highlights.text: Three or four nights between Luxor and Aswan, stopping at the temples of Edfu and Kom Ombo.

name: North Coast & El-Alamein
tagline: Turquoise Mediterranean beaches and a turning point of WWII.
summary: Egypt's Mediterranean shore is where Egyptians go for summer: white sand, clear shallow water and new resort towns. El-Alamein, where the Allies stopped Rommel's advance in 1942, is part of the same coastline.
bestTime: June to September for the beach; spring for sightseeing.

highlights.title: Mediterranean beaches
highlights.text: Soft white sand and calm turquoise water at Marassi, Sidi Abdel Rahman and New Alamein.

highlights.title: El-Alamein war cemeteries
highlights.text: The Commonwealth, German and Italian memorials to the soldiers of the 1942 desert battles.

highlights.title: El-Alamein Military Museum
highlights.text: Maps, uniforms, tanks and the story of the Second Battle of El-Alamein (October–November 1942).

highlights.title: Day trip to Alexandria
highlights.text: The Bibliotheca Alexandrina, the Citadel of Qaitbay and fresh seafood on the Corniche — about two hours away.

name: Sinai
tagline: Red Sea reefs, desert mountains and Bedouin hospitality.
summary: The Sinai peninsula mixes world-class diving with some of the most striking mountain scenery in the Middle East. Choose laid-back Dahab, the sacred peaks of St. Catherine or the resorts of Sharm El Sheikh — or combine all three.
bestTime: March to May and September to November. Mountain nights are cold all winter.

highlights.title: Coral reefs
highlights.text: Some of the richest reefs in the world begin a few metres from the shore.

highlights.title: Sunrise on Mount Sinai
highlights.text: An overnight climb with a Bedouin guide to watch the sun rise over the peaks.

highlights.title: Desert & Bedouin culture
highlights.text: Jeep and camel trips, canyons and tea around the fire in the desert.

gallery.caption: Coral reef in the Red Sea

spots.name: Dahab
spots.text: A relaxed former Bedouin fishing village with a seafront promenade of cafés. Famous for its shore dives and a favourite of backpackers and long-stay travellers.
highlights: The Blue Hole and the Canyon dive sites
Snorkelling at the Lighthouse and Three Pools
Windsurfing and kitesurfing in the Lagoon
Day trips to the Coloured Canyon

spots.name: St. Catherine
spots.tagline: Mount Moses and the desert mountains
spots.text: A small town high in the mountains of South Sinai, home to one of the oldest working Christian monasteries in the world and the trail to the summit of Mount Sinai.
highlights: Night climb of Mount Sinai (Jebel Musa, 2,285 m) for sunrise
St. Catherine's Monastery, built in the 6th century
Mount Catherine — Egypt's highest peak (2,629 m)

spots.name: Sharm El Sheikh
spots.text: Egypt's best-known Red Sea resort town, with large all-inclusive hotels, easy beach access and the protected reefs of Ras Mohammed on its doorstep.
highlights: Boat trips to the reefs of Tiran Island
Naama Bay's promenade, restaurants and nightlife
